subject: Crypto Industry Raining Millions On Candidates That Back Its Favorite Bill
posts:
The crypto industry pours nearly $200 million into 2026 midterm campaigns to back its favored digital asset legislation.
Evidence: FEC filings, PAC donations, Clarity Act lobbying
#Aletheia #Crypto #Politics

Cryptocurrency companies are openly supporting legislative clarity and innovation through standard democratic campaign contributions.
Stated Judgement: (+0.2, 0.0) — Good Preference

A concentrated financial sector is deploying massive capital to secure favorable regulatory loopholes, bypassing broader public financial stability concerns.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Immense campaign spending leverages political access to secure bespoke regulatory exemptions.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.5, z: 3)

- Crypto Industry: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Buying legislative influence for regulatory carve-outs.
- Banking Sector Critics: COND (-0.4, -0.2) — Protecting market share under safety pretexts.
Cryptocurrency interests have contributed nearly $200 million to candidates across party lines to push for the passage of the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act.

The Poison:
Massive financial influx into elections deepens donor sway, turning complex regulatory policy into a highest-bidder auction.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing public market safety (WHERE) with private capital lobbying power (WHO).

Social Physics Analysis:
When single-issue industries flood elections with capital, they use financial leverage as a pretext for public innovation while securing private capture.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map heavy donor spending against stated regulatory reform, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Financial power reshapes legislation to favor capital over safety.

The Unavoidable Truth: Massive campaign spending directly buys legislative priority and influence.

The Unavoidable Lie: Industry political donations are purely motivated by broad civic innovation.

Alethekanon:
Capital concentration masquerades as regulatory progress. Massive lobbying rewrites market rules to favor deep pockets.

Awwthekanon:
It feels discouraging watching huge sums of money steer the laws that affect everyone's financial security, overshadowing everyday voices.

Brothekanon:
Surprise, surprise. Drop two hundred million on campaigns and suddenly your favorite bill is the top priority in Congress.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not wear yourself out to get rich; do not rely on your own cleverness." Proverbs 23:4 FAIL
When wealth dictates the framing of laws, public trust is traded for private advantage.
